In nearby galaxies, the star formation rate (SFR) is observed to
correlate spatially with the distribution of neutral gas, at least to
first order. This is observed using a variety of SFR and gas tracers,
but the quantitative relationship between the two remains poorly
understood. Although it is common to relate SFR to gas surface density
via a power law, the relationship is often more complex. The same
surface density of gas can correspond to dramatically different SFRs
depending on whether it is found in a spiral or irregular galaxy or in
the inner or outer part of a galactic disk. Such variations have
